one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window: Q2 was reported Aug 4 and Q3-25 on Nov 3, so Q3-26 results are most likely the first week of November, after Oct 31. Scheduled or likely items inside the window: (1) Black Pearl Data Hall 2 (35 IT MW) targeted rack-ready Oct 31 [8]; (2) first Barber Lake data-hall rent commencement 'expected during Q4 2026' [5], which could be press-released; (3) possible new HPC lease news at Odessa, Ulysses or Reveille ('multiple interested parties' [10]); this is a right-tail event, and the AWS lease announcement moved the stock about +19%; (4) macro: an FOMC meeting in late October and a 10-yr yield at 5.24% [13], which pressures long-duration, high-beta AI-infrastructure names; (5) continued selling by holder Bitfury (Form 4 Sep 30 [11]), a supply overhang. The stock fell 19% from $19.09 (Sep 22) to $15.46 even after good Barber Lake news, partly on the $359M cost absorption and partly on sector weakness [14]. Short-horizon reversal is weak evidence, so I stay near symmetric: lognormal centred at $15.30 (a slight downward tilt for overhang and rates) with sigma 0.30, a bit below the 112%/3.5 = 32% rule because no earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend: DCF of the three signed leases plus modest pipeline value, $7.85 (40%); SOTP with 6.5% cap rate on 2028 NOI $732M plus $/MW pipeline less $5.5B adjusted net debt, $12.7 (35%); 18x 2028E EBITDA $575M plus pipeline, $12.9 (25%). Blended about $10.81 on 496M fully diluted shares. The current price is pricing in several more leases than are signed.

bear.story: The AI-capex cycle cools or the market sours on neocloud credit (Fluidstack), more overruns or Barber Lake hall slippage beyond Q1-27, no new lease signed in 12 months, and an equity raise or Bitfury selling. The stock re-rates to contracted-value-only, roughly my DCF ex-most-pipeline ($5-9), with a 5.2%+ 10-yr compressing multiples.

base.story: Black Pearl fully delivered by about Mar-27, Barber Lake rent flowing by Q2-27, Stingray rent from Apr/May-27; run-rate NOI near $700M by end-2027. One mid-size lease (Odessa, Ulysses or Reveille) is signed and the market keeps paying ~$1-2B for pipeline above contracted value, so the stock sits roughly flat around $14-17.

bull.story: Two or more new hyperscaler leases including a first phase at a Batch-Zero GW site (Colchis), the AI-infrastructure trade re-accelerates, and the stock moves toward sell-side targets ($26-32) as the market capitalises contracted NOI at a 5.5-6% cap rate and values GW-scale pipeline.

thesis_break_reason: Around $8-9 the market would be valuing CIFR at little more than its signed leases minus $5.5B of debt (my contracted DCF is ~$5-8/share). Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental problem rather than volatility: a tenant default or dispute (Fluidstack, even with the Google backstop), a large further Barber Lake overrun or delay beyond the 120-day termination window in the AWS leases, or a pipeline that cannot be leased or financed.

reasoning: Primary-lane work: I read the Q2-26 10-Q, earnings release, business-update deck and the Sep-24 8-K, plus the Black Pearl and Stingray bond-offering decks, which give lease size, $/MW cost caps, escalators and an annual NOI/amortisation schedule that most recaps skip. Facts: three signed campuses (Black Pearl 216 IT MW to AWS for ~$5.5B over 15 yrs; Stingray 70 IT MW to AWS for ~$2.0B over 15 yrs; Barber Lake to Fluidstack/Google, now extended to 20 yrs, total >$9B). The company projects ~$793M average annual NOI over Oct-26 to Sep-36. Against that: $6.0B of debt, $3.7B of restricted cash that I assume is consumed by remaining construction, a newly disclosed $359M overrun borne by Cipher, ~$113M/yr cash overhead plus ~$120M/yr SBC, and ~496M fully diluted shares. My DCF of the signed leases (8%/9.5% discount, residual at 70% x 10x NOI) plus $1.4B of pipeline gives ~$7.9; SOTP and EV/EBITDA give ~$12.7-12.9; the blend is ~$10.8, below the $15.46 price and well below sell-side targets ($26-32). The market is clearly paying for future leases on a ~4.4 GW pipeline. Lease announcements have historically moved the stock 15-20%, and management says several sites are in active talks, so I do not center the forecast on fundamental value. With 112% realized vol, I use a three-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $7.5 (32%), base $15 (44%), bull $27 (24%), each sigma 0.33-0.45. That gives a median ~$14.4 (slightly below spot, reflecting the fair-value gap, rates at 5.24%, Bitfury overhang and dilution) and a mean ~$16.5 (right skew from lease wins). P(>=$15.46) = 0.45. Research limits: no option data used per the brief; consensus targets taken from press snippets; Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data price targets were unavailable.
